input: This summary recommends that a metered trial be run on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken; the plant engineer owns the trial. The food plant uses 2422 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. A heat-recovery retrofit is projected by the equipment vendor to save 15% of that use, a derived saving of 363 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost is $383k; at an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $33k and the derived simple payback is 11.6 years. It should be noted that the saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the projection is untested at the condition where the refrigeration plant works hardest. A payback beyond a decade, resting on an unmeasured projection, is not really a basis for committing the capital sum. The trade-off is metering and engineering time on one line against a capital commitment that the trial either justifies or removes. The trial would run the retrofit on one line under metering through a full season, so that the saving is measured on the plant's own load, at the plant's own operating pattern, before the decision is taken. What the trial must report is the recovered saving on that line against the same line unmodified, with the summer peak inside the measurement period; a trial that misses the peak would simply repeat the gap in the vendor's case. On the trial result, the capital decision is taken again with a measured figure in place of the projection.
